Like someone changing the house numbers on your street so your post is delivered to them first.
ARP cache poisoning from the device with MAC mac-c7efd6 (its own address is
lan-host-afb302), for example a tool like arpspoof, ettercap or bettercap.
1. Find the device: look up MAC mac-c7efd6 in your switch's MAC address table (or the router's client
list) to get its port or Wi-Fi name, then disconnect it.
2. Check your own ARP cache with
3. As a temporary measure, pin the router:
interface ipv4 add neighbors "Ethernet" lan-host-6c90b4 mac-f75148
4. Enable Dynamic ARP Inspection (with DHCP snooping) and port security on managed switches.
5. Treat passwords typed while this was happening as exposed: change them, and prefer HTTPS/VPN.
Why we think it's an attack
The suspicious MAC answered ARP for 2 different IPs that belong to other devices (lan-host-ffa1cb,
The disputed address lan-host-6c90b4 belongs to the router (default gateway)
The suspicious MAC mac-c7efd6 sent 149 ARP replies nobody asked for
Why not “Two devices are using the same IP address”?
Some signs pointed this way (Both MACs answered the
same ARP question 6 times, which is what two honest devices with the same address do), but they were
outweighed. The stronger evidence: The suspicious MAC answered ARP for 2 different IPs that belong to
other devices (lan-host-ffa1cb, lan-host-6c90b4); The disputed address lan-host-6c90b4 belongs to the
